items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: Alfred Williams stayed there a long time. Jim Robinson stayed there a long time. But uh, Alfred left and went to Texas.

ctx.x: And I wondered if that was before. No, I think that was after they left the Astoria. Mm-hmm.

They would often come down there with me, out to La Vida. Well, I think John, uh, Lee Collins and John Marrero left for, uh, left, uh, a tenor player there. Yeah, they went to Chicago and left him there. And they went to Chicago and left him there. And David Jones stayed there with me a long time. As a matter of fact, he opened up, uh, a teacher school uptown here somewhere. here some way. Alfred Williams stayed there a long time. Jim Robinson stayed there a long time. But uh, Alfred left and went to Texas. And…
Is that the sort of Mexican looking fella? Yeah, yeah, that's him. I think Andy Anderson was talking about that.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Pretty good while, Handy playing with him a good while.

ctx.x: So, who would he have in his dance band when you first joined?

Vernon Gilbert. And me, him, Vernon Gilbert, Tillman. Playing what? Tillman playing bass, you know. Mm-hmm. Bass horn, you know, like he playing the Vernon Gilbert trumpet. You know, clarinet. And, um, well, he had a saxophonian, Handy playing with him. Pretty good while, Handy playing with him a good while. Um, and after Handy stopped playing with him, and I had Harold. Mm-hmm. Harold been playing with him. He was Smitty on piano. And he used the piano, you know what I'm saying? Did he use a guitar player…
That's not the same as Raymond Clifford. No, no.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: Oh, Alfred Whittemey. That's the playing drums.

ctx.x: Did you have a band with Kid Howell and Jim Crow? Yeah. Who else was in that band? Uh,

Miss Howard, Jim Crow, Drew Rubishow. I think John Burrell was playing that, and myself. I don't know how many of those are. Did you have the drums or bass? Yeah, we had drums and trying to sing. Where's the band coming from? I don't know if it's in the... Alfred. Oh, Alfred Whittemey. That's the playing drums. Then Howard and I had a band together.

Yeah, Raymond Brown. He would play. Then Handley, he would get on the drum, you know. Play a waltz, you know, until I come back. Yeah. Then after I left there in 29, around 20, yeah, I don't know, around 27, I played there about a year, 28. Celestine and Ridgely's band broke up then. That's when the band split. Well, I went with Ridgely. See, Ridgely made up a band. See, I went with Ridgely, paid with Ridgely down at Pete Hoyman's place. What do you call it? Planetation? Yeah. Planetation. That's right. I worked…
Shots, Handy, Sales. What did Handy play in those days? Alto and clarinet. Did he play much clarinet then? Oh, lots of clarinet. I can't think of this one. I'm a mic now.
About sales, how did he rate among the guitar players and banjo players?
